image_description: A close-up, low-angle photograph of a large Triceratops skull mounted on display stands in front of a stone building facade. The skull features the characteristic three horns (two long brow horns, one short nasal horn) and a massive solid bony frill. The texture appears to be fossilized bone or a high-fidelity cast, showing weathering and cracks. No body, limbs, or tail are visible; only the head is present.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image clearly displays the iconic triceratops horn configuration: two large supraorbital horns curving forward/upward and a smaller nasal horn. They are structurally sound and correctly positioned relative to the eye sockets.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The frill surface appears solid and continuous. There are visible undulations along the margin that correspond to epoccipitals. The texture is consistent with fossilized bone.
